item.text:
**1B.5 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

**Bottom line:** I found no credible 2024 evidence that Abiy Ahmed used nuclear capability to shield aggression, coercion, or repression. The usable record points the other way: Ethiopia pursued peaceful nuclear cooperation, participated in regional nuclear-science cooperation, and Abiy repeatedly used de-escalatory language on Somalia, the Nile, and the Red Sea. The main limitation is structural: Ethiopia is not known to have a nuclear weapons capability, so the lens is mostly an absence-of-evidence test.

### 2024 Evidence

| Date | Title | Publisher | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

This supports a non-militarized nuclear posture and gives no indication of nuclear cover for aggression. | 1B.5, 1B.3, 1B.4 |
| 2024-09-21 | Ethiopia to Chair AFRA for One Year | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5179100 | Ethiopia took over chairmanship of AFRA, an intergovernmental framework promoting peaceful nuclear science and technology in Africa. This is positive evidence for civilian nuclear engagement, not coercive nuclear signaling. | 1B.5, 1B.4 |
| 2024-02-06 | Ethiopia's leader plays down fears of conflict with Somalia over a planned naval port | Associated Press via CityNews | https://kitchener.citynews.ca/2024/02/06/ethiopias-leader-plays-down-fears-of-conflict-with-somalia-over-a-planned-naval-port/ | Abiy said he had “no intention” of going to war with Somalia and framed peace as mutually beneficial. This is direct evidence against brinkmanship and against using any hypothetical strategic capability as cover for coercion. | 1B.5, 1B.2, 1B.1, 1B.4 |
| 2024-10-31 | Abiy Reaffirms Government’s Commitment for Durable Peace, Security | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5380692 | Abiy said the government “always opts for peace over forceful approach” and emphasized dialogue, forgiveness, and peaceful resolution of conflict. This is supportive evidence for restraint rather than escalation. | 1B.5, 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.1 |
| 2024-10-31 | Ethiopia Pursues Peaceful Access to Red Sea Amid Growing Economy: PM Abiy | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5380659 | Abiy said Ethiopia sought Red Sea access “in a peaceful manner” and that the agenda was “not about confrontation.” This cuts against any reading of coercive shielding behavior. | 1B.5, 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.1 |
| 2024-12-12 | Ethiopia-Somalia Ankara Declaration under facilitation of Republic of Türkiye | Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications | https://www.iletisim.gov.tr/English/haberler/detay/ethiopia-somalia-ankara-declaration-under-facilitation-of-republic-of-turkiye | Ethiopia and Somalia agreed to respect sovereignty, set aside disputes, and cooperate. This is the clearest 2024 de-escalation item and is inconsistent with using nuclear capability as political cover. | 1B.5, 1B.4, 1B.1 |

This is background rather than a 2024 event. | 1B.5, 1B.4 |

### Search gap

- I searched directly for 2024 evidence of nuclear capability, nuclear warning language, and nuclear shielding behavior.
- I found no credible 2024 evidence that Abiy Ahmed possessed or leveraged nuclear weapons capability.
- I also found no credible 2024 source showing him invoking nuclear threats or using nuclear rhetoric to cover conventional aggression or domestic repression.
- The available evidence is instead about peaceful nuclear cooperation and regional de-escalation.

### Assessment

- Best-supported answer: **No evidence that Abiy used nuclear capability to shield aggression in 2024.**
- Strongest positive evidence: peaceful nuclear cooperation and repeated de-escalatory statements.
- Strongest negative context: Ethiopia’s conventional coercive actions in 2024 existed, but they were not nuclear-backed and do not establish this lens.
